system.name: Protego
system.one_liner: an overload-control system that combines credit-based admission control with active synchronization queue management for RPC servers with unpredictable lock contention

components.name: request
components.role: incoming RPC request arriving at the server

components.name: RPC Server
components.role: the example server (using a global mutex) that Protego is combined with

components.name: Blocking Queue Management
components.role: manages the two queues around CPU processing and mutex acquisition, dropping requests that wait too long

components.name: CPU
components.role: processes a dequeued request up to the point where it needs the mutex

components.name: mutex
components.role: the global lock guarding the contended critical section

components.name: Admission control
components.role: decides how many requests to admit using a credit-based scheme informed by observed throughput

components.name: Throughput / Incoming Load chart
components.role: shows how measured throughput responds to incoming load, the signal Protego observes to judge its admission rate

components.name: Credit pool
components.role: the pool of available credits issued to clients to control admitted load

components.name: failure
components.role: output reporting a request dropped by either queue

components.name: response
components.role: output for a request that completed successfully

components.name: credit
components.role: output token issued to the client controlling how much further load it may send

flows.what: incoming RPC request enters the first queue
request dropped after waiting too long before CPU processing
request queued again waiting to acquire the mutex
request dropped at lock-acquisition time (ASQM) to avoid excessive blocking on the critical section
successfully completed request returns a response

content.key_idea: Protego wraps an RPC server with two mechanisms: Blocking Queue Management drops requests that wait too long before CPU processing or mutex acquisition, while Admission control adjusts a credit pool by observing how admission rate affects measured throughput.
content.reading_order: Left to right: a request passes through two drop-capable queues around the CPU and mutex; Admission control's credit pool gates load and reports back.

evidence: Figure 4 illustrates an overview of Protego combined with a simple RPC server that uses a global mutex.
Protego is composed of two main components: an admission controller and an AQM mechanism.
a novel form of AQM that drops requests at lock acquisition time to prevent blocking on a critical section

summary: This figure gives an overview of Protego, an overload-control mechanism shown combined with a simple RPC server that serializes access to a global mutex. Requests enter a 'Blocking Queue Management' panel that queues them before CPU processing and again before mutex acquisition; either queue can time out and drop the request (shown in red), producing a 'failure' output, while requests that complete produce a 'response'. Beside it, an 'Admission control' panel implements a credit-based scheme: it watches a Throughput-vs-Incoming-Load curve to see how its current admission rate affects system performance, then raises or lowers the number of credits in a 'Credit pool' accordingly. Those credits are returned to the client to control how much further load it may send, closing the loop between observed performance and admitted load without relying on any specific overload signal.
